item.research_question: How does the molten salt corrosion behavior of the dual-phase AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy compare to conventional duplex stainless steel 2205 in a NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 environment at temperatures relevant to concentrating solar power systems?
item.material_system: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) and duplex stainless steel 2205 (DS2205)
item.processing_route: Vacuum-arc-melting of high purity constituent elements (99.95 wt.% purity) with multiple re-melts for homogeneity; samples cut to 20 mm × 5 mm × 2 mm, polished to 1200-grit, degreased with acetone, and dried; corrosion tests performed in a custom tube furnace with 20 mm salt melt depth at 450 °C and 650 °C for 24 h
item.test_conditions: Molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 salt (45.4 wt.% MgCl2, 33 wt.% NaCl, 21.6 wt.% KCl) at 450 °C and 650 °C; immersion for 24 h; electrochemical measurements including OCP (1 h stabilization) and potentiodynamic polarization (-0.5 to 1.5 V at 1 mV/s)
key_findings: Corrosion rate of AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 was ~1 mm/year at 450 °C compared to ~8 mm/year for DS2205.
Corrosion rate of AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 was ~9 mm/year at 650 °C compared to ~20 mm/year for DS2205.
Mass loss for DS2205 at 650 °C was ~69 mg/cm² after 24 h, while AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 was ~38 mg/cm².
Cr depletion depth in AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 at 650 °C was ~50 μm, whereas DS2205 showed ~300 μm.
The Volta potential difference between phases was ~50 mV for AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 and ~35 mV for DS2205.
Selective dissolution occurred in the BCC phase (B2 in EHEA, α-Ferrite in DS2205) due to micro-galvanic coupling.
Work function increased with temperature for AlCoCrFeNi 2.1, indicating the FCC-L12 phase acted as a barrier.
item.mechanism: Selective dissolution of the BCC phase is driven by micro-galvanic coupling with the nobler FCC phase, evidenced by Volta potential differences. In AlCoCrFeNi 2.1, Al acts as a sacrificial element forming a redox buffer (Al/AlCl3 and Cr/CrCl2) that reduces Cr dissolution and allows Co/Ni enrichment in the surface layer, while the FCC-L12 phase acts as a protective barrier against further oxidation.
item.limitations: A detailed evaluation of the effect of moisture content on corrosion behavior has not been performed in the current study.
item.future_work: The effect of moisture content on corrosion behavior is part of a future study.
quotes: The EHEA showed a significantly lower corrosion rate of ~1 mm/year at 450 °C compared to ~8 mm/year for DS2205.
This was attributed to micro-galvanic coupling between the two phases in each alloy that was measured in terms of Volta potential difference using a scanning kelvin probe.
Additionally, the work function increased with increasing temperature for AlCoCrFeNi 2.1, indicating that the FCC-L1 2 phase acted as a barrier against further oxidation.
